1	package github
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5	
6		"github.com/harnaas/harnaas/cmd/harnaas/cli/manifest"
7		"github.com/harnaas/harnaas/cmd/harnaas/cli/source"
8	)
9	
10	// Every diagnostic here names the asset as well as the repository, because the
11	// person reading it is looking for the line to edit. A repository and a ref
12	// alone describe the failure accurately and say nothing about where it came
13	// from — one `sources` entry is referenced by any number of assets, and the
14	// manifest is what the reader has open.
15	
16	// UnknownRefError reports a ref the repository does not have.
17	//
18	// It is a distinct type rather than a message because an unknown ref is the one
19	// ref failure that is always a manifest edit: the repository answered, harnaas
20	// reached it, and the name is simply not there.
21	type UnknownRefError struct {
22		// AssetID is the asset whose source declared the ref.
23		AssetID string
24	
25		// Repository is the `owner/repository` pair the manifest declared.
26		Repository string
27	
28		// Ref is the ref as written, so a typo is visible in the message rather
29		// than only in the file.
30		Ref string
31	}
32	
33	// Error states the problem and then the fix, as every user-facing diagnostic
34	// does.
35	func (e *UnknownRefError) Error() string {
36		return fmt.Sprintf(
37			"the asset %q asks for %s at %q, which that repository has no tag, branch or commit for\n\n"+
38				"Change the ref after @ in %s to one that exists in %s, or pin the commit identifier directly.",
39			e.AssetID, e.Repository, e.Ref, manifest.FileName, e.Repository,
40		)
41	}
42	
43	// RefLookupError reports a ref lookup that could not be made at all.
44	//
45	// A repository that is private, renamed, deleted or simply unreachable all
46	// arrive here, and they are one diagnostic rather than four because git's own
47	// message is the part that tells them apart and harnaas has nothing to add to
48	// it. What harnaas contributes is which asset was being resolved.
49	type RefLookupError struct {
50		// AssetID is the asset whose source was being resolved.
51		AssetID string
52	
53		// Repository is the `owner/repository` pair the manifest declared.
54		Repository string
55	
56		// Ref is the ref as written. It is empty where the request declared none.
57		Ref string
58	
59		// Remote is the Git remote harnaas asked, held raw and redacted where the
60		// message is built — the same rule the transport diagnostics follow, so
61		// redaction is a property of the type rather than a step a caller
62		// constructing one has to remember.
63		Remote string
64	
65		// Err is git's own failure, kept so a caller can still recognize a
66		// cancelled run through errors.Is.
67		Err error
68	}
69	
70	// Error states the problem and then the fix.
71	func (e *RefLookupError) Error() string {
72		return fmt.Sprintf(
73			"could not resolve %s for the asset %q against %s: %s\n\n"+
74				"Check that the repository exists and that this machine can read it — a private repository is resolved with the Git credentials already configured on this machine — then run harnaas install again.",
75			e.describeRef(), e.AssetID, source.RedactURL(e.Remote), e.Err,
76		)
77	}
78	
79	// Unwrap keeps git's failure inspectable, which is what lets an interrupted run
80	// still be recognized as a cancellation rather than as a repository problem.
81	func (e *RefLookupError) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
82	
83	// describeRef names what was being resolved, which is a ref where the manifest
84	// declared one and the default branch where it did not.
85	func (e *RefLookupError) describeRef() string {
86		if e.Ref == "" {
87			return "the default branch of " + e.Repository
88		}
89		return fmt.Sprintf("%q in %s", e.Ref, e.Repository)
90	}
91	
92	// ArchiveRetrievalError reports an archive that could not be retrieved, or that
93	// arrived as something no source could be built from.
94	//
95	// The transport layer already says what went wrong — a host that refused, a
96	// status the forge answered, a body past the ceiling — and says nothing about
97	// where the request came from. This is that half. The commit is named as well as
98	// the repository because it is a fact the manifest does not contain: an author
99	// reading "acme/assets is unreachable" learns nothing about which commit their
100	// ref had already resolved to, and that is what the retry, the cache entry and
101	// the lockfile line are all keyed by.
102	type ArchiveRetrievalError struct {
103		// AssetID is the asset whose source was being resolved.
104		AssetID string
105	
106		// Repository is the `owner/repository` pair the manifest declared.
107		Repository string
108	
109		// Commit is the commit the declared ref resolved to, which is the commit the
110		// archive was asked for.
111		Commit string
112	
113		// Err is the retrieval failure. It is kept whole so a cancelled run is still
114		// recognizable through errors.Is, and only its problem is quoted: it carries
115		// a fix of its own, and a message offering two leaves the reader deciding
116		// which one is theirs.
117		Err error
118	}
119	
120	// Error states the problem and then the fix.
121	func (e *ArchiveRetrievalError) Error() string {
122		return fmt.Sprintf(
123			"could not retrieve %s at commit %s for the asset %q: %s\n\n"+
124				"Check that the repository is readable from this machine and that the ref %s declares still resolves to a commit it has, then run harnaas install again.",
125			e.Repository, e.Commit, e.AssetID, source.Problem(e.Err), manifest.FileName,
126		)
127	}
128	
129	// Unwrap keeps the retrieval failure inspectable, so an interrupted run is still
130	// a cancellation rather than an unreachable repository.
131	func (e *ArchiveRetrievalError) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
132	
133	// AuthorizationError reports a repository the forge would not let this request
134	// read.
135	//
136	// It is separate from [ArchiveRetrievalError] because the edit that fixes it is
137	// not in the manifest: the source is declared correctly, the ref resolved, and
138	// what failed is the credential the archive was asked for with. A message
139	// pointing at `harnaas.json` would send the reader to change a file that is
140	// already right, so this one names the token instead — which variable it came
141	// from, or every variable it could have come from when there was none.
142	//
143	// The type deliberately has no field a token could be put in. Naming the origin
144	// is what makes the message actionable, and holding the value is what would
145	// eventually put it in a log.
146	type AuthorizationError struct {
147		// AssetID is the asset whose source was being resolved.
148		AssetID string
149	
150		// Repository is the `owner/repository` pair the manifest declared.
151		Repository string
152	
153		// Commit is the commit the declared ref resolved to.
154		Commit string
155	
156		// TokenOrigin names where the token harnaas presented was read from, and is
157		// empty where the request was made without one.
158		TokenOrigin string
159	
160		// Err is the refusal the forge answered with, kept whole so a caller can
161		// still inspect the status, and quoted only for its problem.
162		Err error
163	}
164	
165	// Error states the problem and then the fix.
166	func (e *AuthorizationError) Error() string {
167		if e.TokenOrigin != "" {
168			return fmt.Sprintf(
169				"the asset %q could not read %s at commit %s: %s, and harnaas made that request with the token in %s\n\n"+
170					"Check that the token in %s can read %s and has not expired, then run harnaas install again.",
171				e.AssetID, e.Repository, e.Commit, source.Problem(e.Err), e.TokenOrigin,
172				e.TokenOrigin, e.Repository,
173			)
174		}
175	
176		return fmt.Sprintf(
177			"the asset %q could not read %s at commit %s: %s, and harnaas made that request without a token because none of %s was set\n\n"+
178				"Set one of them to a token that can read %s, then run harnaas install again. A private repository is not readable without one, and an unauthenticated request also meets the forge's rate limit far sooner.",
179			e.AssetID, e.Repository, e.Commit, source.Problem(e.Err), describeTokenChain(),
180			e.Repository,
181		)
182	}
183	
184	// Unwrap keeps the refusal inspectable, so a caller can still recognize the
185	// status the forge answered with.
186	func (e *AuthorizationError) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
187	
188	// GitUnavailableError reports that harnaas could not run git at all.
189	//
190	// It is separate from every other lookup failure because it is the one that is
191	// not about the manifest, the network or the repository: nothing the author
192	// could write in `harnaas.json` would fix it, so a message pointing at the file
193	// would send them to edit a file that is already correct.
194	type GitUnavailableError struct {
195		// Err is the failure that reported git missing, kept for logs and for a
196		// caller matching on exec.ErrNotFound.
197		Err error
198	}
199	
200	// Error states the problem and then the fix.
201	func (e *GitUnavailableError) Error() string {
202		return fmt.Sprintf(
203			"harnaas resolves a %s source's ref by running git, which is not installed on this machine\n\n"+
204				"Install git and run harnaas install again, or pin each %s source to a full commit identifier, which needs no lookup.",
205			manifest.SourceKindGitHub, manifest.SourceKindGitHub,
206		)
207	}
208	
209	// Unwrap keeps the underlying lookup failure inspectable.
210	func (e *GitUnavailableError) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }

19	// surface is: a test that asked the package which errors it declares would agree
20	// with any set. Adding one is therefore two edits, and the second one is where
21	// somebody confirms the new message names the asset and leaks nothing.
22	func TestEveryRefFailureIsShapedProblemThenFix(t *testing.T) {
23		t.Parallel()
24	
25		// The remote is built with a credential in it, which harnaas never does
26		// itself — the point is that a diagnostic printing one would be the type's
27		// mistake and not the caller's.
28		const remote = "REDACTED"

30		failures := map[string]error{

32			"lookup refused": &github.RefLookupError{

34				Repository: "acme/assets",
35				Ref:        "v1.2.0",
36				Remote:     remote,
37				Err:        errors.New("fatal: repository not found"),
38			},
39			"git unavailable": &github.GitUnavailableError{Err: errors.New(`exec: "git": executable file not found in $PATH`)},
40			// The cause is a real transport diagnostic rather than a plain error,
41			// because the credential is redacted by the type that holds the URL —
42			// so what this case proves is that quoting a cause's problem carries
43			// that redaction with it rather than reaching around it.
44			"archive retrieval": &github.ArchiveRetrievalError{
45				AssetID:    "review",
46				Repository: "acme/assets",
47				Commit:     "9f2a1c4e8b7d6a5f4e3c2b1a0987654321fedcba",
48				Err:        &source.FetchError{URL: remote, Err: errors.New("no such host")},
49			},

51				AssetID:     "review",
52				Repository:  "acme/assets",
53				Commit:      "9f2a1c4e8b7d6a5f4e3c2b1a0987654321fedcba",
54				TokenOrigin: "HARNAAS_GITHUB_TOKEN",
55				Err:         &source.StatusError{URL: remote, StatusCode: 403, Status: "403 Forbidden"},

61				Err:        &source.StatusError{URL: remote, StatusCode: 404, Status: "404 Not Found"},
62			},

42	// resolveRequest builds a request for one asset at a path within the source.
43	func resolveRequest(id, ref, path string) source.Request {
44		req := request(ref)

50	// archiveOf builds the gzipped tar a forge serves, wrapping every named file in
51	// the archive's single top-level directory.
52	func archiveOf(tb testing.TB, files map[string]string) []byte {
53		tb.Helper()
54	
55		var buffer bytes.Buffer
56		gz := gzip.NewWriter(&buffer)
57		writer := tar.NewWriter(gz)
58	
59		for _, name := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(files)) {
60			require.NoError(tb, writer.WriteHeader(&tar.Header{
61				Name:     wrapper + name,
62				Typeflag: tar.TypeReg,
63				Size:     int64(len(files[name])),
64				Mode:     0o644,
65			}))
66			_, err := writer.Write([]byte(files[name]))
67			require.NoError(tb, err)
68		}
69	
70		require.NoError(tb, writer.Close())
71		require.NoError(tb, gz.Close())
72		return buffer.Bytes()
73	}

101	// asked for, which is how "fetched at most once" is asserted as a number rather
102	// than inferred from a result that happens to be right.
103	type countingFetcher struct {

107		body        []byte

1	// Package github resolves `github` sources: the ref a manifest pinned becomes
2	// the commit it names, and that commit's repository archive becomes the files
3	// an asset installs.
4	//
5	// Names are resolved with Git and bytes are moved over HTTPS, and the split is
6	// the whole design. `git ls-remote` goes through whatever credential helper the
7	// user already configured, so a private repository resolves without harnaas
8	// inventing an authentication story of its own, and that path has no API rate
9	// limit for a CI job to exhaust. The archive endpoint is then one request per
10	// repository and commit rather than one request per file, which is what makes a
11	// skill — a directory of documents — cost the same as a rule.
12	//
13	// Resolution is kept separate from retrieval for a second reason: the lockfile
14	// records what was *asked for* alongside what it *resolved to*, because "the
15	// installed files still match the commit" and "the tag now points somewhere
16	// else" are two different questions and `lint` asks them separately.
17	package github
18	
19	// remoteHost is the forge this kind speaks to, and the only place its name is
20	// spelled: a message, a Git remote and an archive URL all read it from here, so
21	// they cannot come to disagree about which host a `github` source means.
22	const remoteHost = "github.com"
23	
24	// remoteURL is the Git remote for an `owner/repository` pair.
25	//
26	// It is built rather than taken from the manifest, which is what keeps a
27	// declared source from naming a host harnaas never agreed to talk to. The
28	// repository arrives already checked for shape by the manifest grammar, so this
29	// is assembly and not validation.
30	func remoteURL(repository string) string {
31		return "https://" + remoteHost + "/" + repository + ".git"
32	}

12	// Content arrives as one archive per repository and commit, never as one request
13	// per file. A skill is a directory of documents, so a per-file route would spend
14	// a listing plus a request per file against a budget a CI job installing a
15	// handful of assets exhausts — and would give the cache a set of files to
16	// reconcile instead of one immutable object named by the commit it is of.
17	//
18	// The consequence is this file: several assets legitimately name different
19	// subtrees of one repository at one commit, so retrieval has to be asked for per
20	// asset and performed once. The memory of what has already been fetched is per
21	// run, which is why the source contract registers a constructor rather than a
22	// value — a memo shared between runs would either leak content into a later one
23	// or need a global to hold it.
24	
25	// archiveHost is the endpoint archives are fetched from, and the only place its
26	// name is spelled.
27	//
28	// It is the API's tarball endpoint rather than the content host directly,
29	// because that is the documented route that takes an authorization header — the
30	// one a private repository needs, and the reason the fetcher follows a bounded
31	// redirect chain: the endpoint answers with a signed URL on the content host,
32	// whose query string carries the grant that [source.RedactURL] exists to drop.
33	const archiveHost = "api.github.com"
34	
35	// archiveURL is the archive of one repository at one commit.
36	//
37	// The commit is used rather than the ref the manifest declared, so the URL names
38	// an object that cannot change under it — which is what makes the response
39	// content-addressable and the same archive reusable for every asset that
40	// resolved to it.
41	func archiveURL(repository, commit string) string {
42		return "https://" + archiveHost + "/repos/" + repository + "/tarball/" + commit
43	}
44	
45	// archiveFetcher retrieves the whole body at a URL, presenting a credential
46	// where the run has one.
47	//
48	// It is a parameter rather than a call for the reason [gitRunner] is: a
49	// resolution has to be exercisable without a network, and the fetcher's own
50	// rules — https only, no destination on this machine — mean a test server cannot
51	// stand in for the forge. The production value is [source.Fetcher.Fetch], which
52	// is the only way harnaas makes an HTTP request at all.
53	type archiveFetcher func(ctx context.Context, url string, credential source.Credential) ([]byte, error)
54	
55	// archiveKey identifies one archive: a repository and the commit its content is
56	// of.
57	//
58	// The commit and not the ref, because two assets pinned to `v1.2.0` and to the
59	// commit that tag names are the same fetch, and the ref is what resolution has
60	// already spent. The credential is not part of the key because it is resolved
61	// once for the whole run: two retrievals within one run are made as the same
62	// identity by construction.
63	type archiveKey struct {
64		repository string
65		commit     string
66	}
67	
68	// errNotCached reports an archive an offline run needs and this machine has
69	// never fetched.
70	//
71	// It is kind-neutral and names no asset, for the reason every remembered
72	// retrieval failure is: the memo holds what the retrieval answered and knows
73	// nothing about which asset reads it, and the asset a diagnostic names is the
74	// one that read it.
75	var errNotCached = errors.New("this machine has no cached archive for that commit")
76	
77	// archives is one run's memory of the archives it has retrieved.
78	type archives struct {
79		fetch archiveFetcher
80	
81		// cache is what earlier runs left on this machine. It is consulted after
82		// the run's own memo and before the network, which is the order the two
83		// memories are cheap in — and a nil one is the caller's bypass, so there is
84		// no second code path for a run that must not read it.
85		cache *source.ArchiveCache
86	
87		// offline is a run that may read those two memories and nothing else. It
88		// belongs here rather than at the fetch call site because this is where the
89		// last memory runs out: the offline rule is exactly "when the cache does not
90		// have it, that is the answer".
91		offline bool
92	
93		// mu guards fetched, and is held only while the slot for a key is found or
94		// created — never across the retrieval itself, so one repository's fetch
95		// does not queue behind another's.
96		mu      sync.Mutex
97		fetched map[archiveKey]*fetchedArchive
98	}
99	
100	// newArchives returns an empty memo retrieving through fetch, under the run's
101	// own choices about the cache it may read and whether it may fetch at all.
102	func newArchives(fetch archiveFetcher, opts source.RunOptions) *archives {
103		return &archives{
104			fetch:   fetch,
105			cache:   opts.Cache,
106			offline: opts.Offline,
107			fetched: map[archiveKey]*fetchedArchive{},
108		}
109	}
110	
111	// fetchedArchive is one archive's slot in the memo: the retrieval, performed at
112	// most once, and whatever it produced.
113	type fetchedArchive struct {
114		once sync.Once
115		body []byte
116		err  error
117	}
118	
119	// get returns the archive for a repository at a commit, retrieving it the first
120	// time it is asked for and not again.
121	//
122	// A retrieval that failed is remembered as well as one that succeeded. The next
123	// asset referencing the same repository would meet the same host and the same
124	// answer, so asking again would multiply one outage by the number of assets
125	// declared against it — and the caller attributes the remembered failure to its
126	// own asset, so the second asset's diagnostic still names the second asset.
127	func (a *archives) get(ctx context.Context, repository, commit string, credential source.Credential) ([]byte, error) {
128		key := archiveKey{repository: repository, commit: commit}
129	
130		a.mu.Lock()
131		entry, known := a.fetched[key]
132		if !known {
133			entry = &fetchedArchive{}
134			a.fetched[key] = entry
135		}
136		a.mu.Unlock()
137	
138		entry.once.Do(func() {
139			entry.body, entry.err = a.retrieve(ctx, repository, commit, credential)
140		})
141	
142		return entry.body, entry.err
143	}
144	
145	// retrieve produces one archive, from what an earlier run left on this machine
146	// if it is still usable and from the forge otherwise.
147	//
148	// A cache miss and a damaged entry are the same event here, because the cache
149	// answers with content or with nothing at all — a store that could fail a run
150	// would be a performance feature costing correctness. Only a fetch that
151	// succeeded is filed, so a failure is never cached as though it were content.
152	func (a *archives) retrieve(ctx context.Context, repository, commit string, credential source.Credential) ([]byte, error) {
153		key := source.ArchiveKey{
154			Kind:       manifest.SourceKindGitHub,
155			Repository: repository,
156			Commit:     commit,
157		}
158	
159		if body, cached := a.cache.Lookup(ctx, key); cached {
160			return body, nil
161		}
162	
163		// An offline run stops here, and stops without a request rather than with
164		// one that fails: a machine that is offline because it has no route out
165		// would answer a fetch with a timeout eventually, and eventually is not an
166		// answer. The miss is remembered like any other retrieval failure, so a
167		// second asset of the same repository is not made to wait for the same
168		// nothing — and is still told about itself.
169		if false {
170			return nil, errNotCached
171		}
172	
173		body, err := a.fetch(ctx, archiveURL(repository, commit), credential)
174		if err != nil {
175			return nil, err
176		}
177	
178		a.cache.Store(ctx, key, body)
179		return body, nil
180	}

1	package github

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"net/http"
7	
8		"github.com/harnaas/harnaas/cmd/harnaas/cli/manifest"
9		"github.com/harnaas/harnaas/cmd/harnaas/cli/source"
10	)
11	
12	// Kind resolves every `github` source of one install run.
13	//
14	// It is built per run rather than registered as a value because it holds the
15	// run's archives: several assets naming different subtrees of one repository at
16	// one commit share a single retrieval, and that memory is only correct for as
17	// long as the run that made it.
18	type Kind struct {
19		run      gitRunner
20		archives *archives
21	
22		// credential is the run's token, read from the environment chain once at
23		// construction rather than per retrieval. A run is one identity: reading the
24		// chain per asset would let a variable changed mid-run split one install
25		// into two identities, and would make "which token was this?" a question
26		// with a different answer for each diagnostic.
27		credential source.Credential
28	
29		// offline is the run's answer to whether the network may be reached, held
30		// here as well as in the archive memo because a resolution makes two kinds
31		// of request and this is where the first one is decided.
32		offline bool
33	}
34	
35	// New returns the kind for one install run.
36	//
37	// It is what the source registry registers, and the fetcher it builds is the
38	// only way harnaas makes an HTTP request — so every transport rule applies here
39	// by there being no second route to a request.
40	func New(opts source.RunOptions) source.Kind {
41		return newKind(runGit, source.NewFetcher().Fetch, ambientCredential(), opts)
42	}
43	
44	// newKind is [New] with the git invocation, the retrieval and the credential as
45	// parameters, so a whole resolution is exercisable with neither a network, a
46	// repository nor a token in the environment the suite runs under. The run's own
47	// choices arrive as the options they arrive as everywhere else, so a field added
48	// to them reaches this kind without another parameter.
49	func newKind(run gitRunner, fetch archiveFetcher, credential source.Credential, opts source.RunOptions) *Kind {
50		return &Kind{
51			run:        run,
52			archives:   newArchives(fetch, opts),
53			credential: credential,
54			offline:    opts.Offline,
55		}
56	}
57	
58	// Resolve produces one asset's content and provenance.
59	//
60	// The three steps are deliberately separate: the declared ref becomes a commit
61	// before anything is fetched, the commit's archive is retrieved at most once per
62	// run, and the subtree the asset names is taken out of it. Every failure is
63	// attributed to the asset, and none of them returns a resolved source — an empty
64	// one would converge to deleting every file the asset had installed, which is
65	// why [source.NewResolved] refuses one and why nothing here builds a [source.Resolved]
66	// by any other route.
67	func (k *Kind) Resolve(ctx context.Context, req source.Request) (*source.Resolved, error) {
68		resolution, err := k.resolution(ctx, req)
69		if err != nil {
70			return nil, err
71		}
72	
73		archive, err := k.archives.get(ctx, req.Source.Repository, resolution.Commit, k.credential)
74		if err != nil {
75			return nil, k.retrievalFailure(req, resolution.Commit, err)
76		}
77	
78		content, err := source.ExtractSubtree(archive, req.Asset.Ref.Path, source.ArchiveSubject{
79			AssetID: req.Asset.ID,
80			Source:  req.Source.String(),
81			Commit:  resolution.Commit,
82		})
83		if err != nil {
84			return nil, err
85		}
86	
87		resolved, err := source.NewResolved(source.Provenance{
88			Kind:   manifest.SourceKindGitHub,
89			Source: req.Source.String(),
90			// The ref is recorded beside the commit and never collapsed into it:
91			// "the installed files still match the commit" and "the tag now points
92			// somewhere else" are the two questions lint asks separately.
93			RequestedRef:   req.Source.Ref,
94			ResolvedCommit: resolution.Commit,
95			Mutable:        resolution.Mutable,
96		}, content)
97		if err != nil {
98			return nil, k.retrievalFailure(req, resolution.Commit, err)
99		}
100	
101		return resolved, nil
102	}
103	
104	// resolution turns the declared ref into the commit it names, by the one route
105	// the run has: the remote where the network is available, and the ref itself
106	// where it is not.
107	//
108	// The branch is here rather than inside the lookup so that an offline run makes
109	// no request at all — a lookup that decided to refuse would still be a lookup,
110	// and "no ref lookup is attempted" is the property offline mode is asked for.
111	func (k *Kind) resolution(ctx context.Context, req source.Request) (RefResolution, error) {
112		if false {
113			return resolveRefOffline(req)
114		}
115	
116		return resolveRef(ctx, k.run, remoteURL(req.Source.Repository), req)
117	}
118	
119	// retrievalFailure attributes a retrieval that produced no usable archive to the
120	// asset that asked for it.
121	//
122	// A refusal is separated from every other failure here rather than in the memo,
123	// because the memo holds what the transport answered and nothing about which
124	// asset read it — and because the credential is the run's, not the archive's. A
125	// second asset meeting the remembered refusal therefore gets a message naming
126	// itself and the same token.
127	func (k *Kind) retrievalFailure(req source.Request, commit string, err error) error {
128		// An offline miss is checked first because it is not a failure of the
129		// retrieval: nothing was asked, so there is no host, status or cause to
130		// report, and the only fix is a run with the network available.
131		if errors.Is(err, errNotCached) {
132			return &OfflineArchiveError{
133				AssetID:    req.Asset.ID,
134				Repository: req.Source.Repository,
135				Commit:     commit,
136			}
137		}
138	
139		var status *source.StatusError
140		if errors.As(err, &status) && deniesAccess(status.StatusCode) {
141			return &AuthorizationError{
142				AssetID:     req.Asset.ID,
143				Repository:  req.Source.Repository,
144				Commit:      commit,
145				TokenOrigin: k.credential.Origin,
146				Err:         err,
147			}
148		}
149	
150		return &ArchiveRetrievalError{
151			AssetID:    req.Asset.ID,
152			Repository: req.Source.Repository,
153			Commit:     commit,
154			Err:        err,
155		}
156	}
157	
158	// deniesAccess reports whether a status is the forge declining to serve this
159	// request rather than a failure of any other kind.
160	//
161	// Not found is one of them, which is not the obvious reading. GitHub answers 404
162	// rather than 403 for a repository the request may not see, so that a stranger
163	// cannot learn a private repository exists by asking — and by the time an
164	// archive is fetched, ref resolution has already proved that the repository
165	// exists and holds this commit. It proved it over Git, with the credentials the
166	// user's Git configuration supplies, which are not the token this request
167	// carries. A "not found" here is therefore the forge declining to admit to
168	// harnaas's *HTTP* identity what it just admitted to its Git one.
169	func deniesAccess(status int) bool {
170		switch status {
171		case http.StatusUnauthorized, http.StatusForbidden, http.StatusNotFound:
172			return true
173		default:
174			return false
175		}
176	}

### An offline run refuses a name, and refuses it without asking

Offline is the second field on `source.RunOptions`, settled at the same seam the cache is, because a
run is offline for every kind or for none. What it forbids is a request of *any* kind, which is two
different requests: the archive, and the lookup that turns a ref into a commit. The archive half is
the cache running out — a miss becomes a refusal rather than a fetch, remembered by the in-run memo
like every other retrieval failure so a second asset of one repository is not made to wait for the
same nothing, and still named after the asset that read it. The ref half is not the cache's business
at all: `v1.2.0` and `main` are names in somebody else's repository, and what they point at today is
a fact this machine can only be told. So a name fails offline, and the branch sits above the lookup
rather than inside it — a lookup that decided to refuse would still be a lookup, and no lookup is the
property that was asked for. A full commit identifier resolves offline exactly as it does online,
which is also how the lockfile's recorded commit will resolve once `install` feeds one in: it is a
commit identifier, so it needs no new offline path.

Serving whatever archive this machine happens to hold for a repository is the one answer offline
mode exists to refuse — it installs a commit the manifest never asked for and reports it as the one
it did. Skipping the asset and reporting it unchanged are the same failure by a quieter route. An
offline miss is therefore its own diagnostic rather than a retrieval failure: nothing was asked, so
there is no host, status or cause to quote, and the remedy is one run with the network rather than a
line in `harnaas.json` to change.

**What landed — offline resolution (task 3.10):**

- `source.RunOptions.Offline` sits beside `Cache` and is settled once at `Registry.NewResolver`, so a run is offline for every kind or for none.
- The github kind's archive memo (`cmd/harnaas/cli/source/github/archive.go:169`) turns a cache miss into `errNotCached` instead of a fetch — kind-neutral, remembered like any other retrieval failure so a second asset of one repository doesn't re-derive it, and wrapped per caller so each asset's diagnostic names itself.
- Ref resolution branches *above* the lookup (`kind.go:111`): a full commit identifier resolves as it does online, and a tag, branch or absent ref becomes `OfflineRefError` with no `git ls-remote` invoked at all — a lookup that decided to refuse would still be a lookup.
- Two new diagnostics: `OfflineRefError` (the ref is not known to be wrong, so it is not reported as unknown) and `OfflineArchiveError` (nothing was asked, so there is no host or status to quote and the remedy is one networked run, not a manifest edit). `describeRef` is now one function shared with `RefLookupError` so an absent ref is described identically in both.

**Verification:** disabling each offline branch failed 6 tests (including all four ref shapes and the uncached-archive case), so the new tests assert the absence of a request rather than a result that happens to be right.

**Note on the spec's "cached resolution":** a name has no offline answer today because nothing records ref→commit yet. When section 9's lockfile feeds one in it will be a full commit identifier, which this path already resolves without a lookup — so no new offline logic is owed there; task 10.15 is just the wiring.
